result.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers
result.summary: Feeding each position's top-layer hidden state back into the next position's input improves Transformer performance. However, this feedback breaks speculative decoding, since verifying a drafted token requires the top-layer state from its preceding position, which forces the draft to rely on an approximate stand-in. Training the model to adapt to this stand-in can lower the exact-decoding performance ceiling, while using it at inference time further introduces approximation error. We propose Feedback Shortcut to address both bottlenecks. First, state alignment trains a lightweight projection from multi-token prediction head states to stand-ins, leaving base model training untouched. Second, pipelined correction re-evaluates each draft using its predecessor's newly computed state, a much closer proxy to true feedback. Running this correction inside the verification pass of subsequent drafts improves accuracy with zero extra calls. Across 135M and 780M scales, Feedback Shortcut stays within $10^{-4}$ bits per byte of the exact-decoding ceiling on Paloma and accelerates decoding by 2.4-2.8x with about 2% more training compute than the latent feedback Transformer. At large batch sizes, skipping correction still preserves Transformer speed and over 80% of latent feedback's gains.

AI.brief_summary: 针对把上一层顶层隐状态回灌到下一位置输入的 latent feedback Transformer，提出 Feedback Shortcut：用状态对齐训练轻量投影以生成可替代 draft 的近似状态，并在验证阶段流水线修正，使投机解码在几乎不损失精确解码质量的前提下加速 2.4–2.8 倍。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文讨论的正是循环隐状态反馈下「真实状态 vs 近似替身」的误差与验证期重算，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态更新的缓存近似、并行草拟与验证修正是否会歪曲推理状态。
